quote: Theorem 1. For two parallel systems with component lifetimes being distributed as (X1, X2) ∼ MOE(λ1, λ2, λ3) and (Y1, Y2) ∼ MOE(µ1, µ2, λ3), the following implication holds: ((λ1 + λ3)−1, (λ2 + λ3)−1) ⪰^m ((µ1 + λ3)−1, (µ2 + λ3)−1) ⇒ X2:2 ≥mrl Y2:2.
family: Marshall–Olkin bivariate exponential MOE(λ1, λ2, λ3): F̄(x1,x2) = exp{−(λ1 x1 + λ2 x2 + λ3(x1 ∨ x2))}, common shock λ3
compared: reciprocal rate pairs ((λ1+λ3)^{-1},(λ2+λ3)^{-1}) vs ((µ1+λ3)^{-1},(µ2+λ3)^{-1}) under majorization

hypotheses.formal: majorization of reciprocal-rate vectors (a ⪰^m b per Definition 2(i))

ambiguity: Majorization glyph is ⪰^m (verified on rendered PDF p.6); pdftotext drops the symbol. Pass B's '≺^m' reverses the hypothesis.
adjudication: adjudicated: Prints ((λ1+λ3)^-1,(λ2+λ3)^-1) ⪰^m ((µ1+λ3)^-1,(µ2+λ3)^-1) ⇒ X2:2 >=mrl Y2:2 — A's ⪰^m correct, B mi

quote: Theorem 2. For η ∈ Θn(θ), we have R(X, n) ≥st R(Y, n).
model: other: sample range R(X,n) = Xn:n − X1:n
family: independent exponentials Exp(θi) (X) vs Exp(ηi) (Y), ordered hazard-rate vectors
compared: hazard rate vectors θ vs η with η ∈ Θn(θ)

hypotheses.text: η ∈ Θn(θ) = {η = (η1,...,ηn) ∈ En+ : θ ⪰^p η and θk ≥ ηk for k = 2,...,n}
hypotheses.formal: θ p-majorizes η plus θk >= ηk componentwise for k>=2

ambiguity: Θn uses θ ⪰^p η (p-majorization, Definition 2(iii)); B's 'θ ≺ η' reverses it.
adjudication: adjudicated: Prints η ∈ Θn(θ) ⇒ R(X,n) >=st R(Y,n), with Θn defined by θ ⪰^p η; A's direction correct, B flipped

quote: Theorem 3. For η ∈ Ωn(θ), we have R(X, n) ≥rh R(Y, n).
model: other: sample range R(X,n) = Xn:n − X1:n
family: independent exponentials Exp(θi) (X) vs Exp(ηi) (Y), ordered hazard-rate vectors
compared: hazard rate vectors θ vs η with η ∈ Ωn(θ)

hypotheses.text: η ∈ Ωn(θ) = {η = (η1,...,ηn) ∈ En+ : θ ⪰^w η and θk ≥ ηk for k = 2,...,n}
hypotheses.formal: θ weakly majorizes η plus θk >= ηk componentwise for k>=2

ambiguity: Ωn uses θ ⪰^w η (weak majorization, Definition 2(ii)); B's 'θ ≺^w η' reverses it.
